page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no marginal notes. Below the text is a catchword at the right.

main_text.p: fensæ fuit. Graue autem est,fuijpsius,& reuerentiæ conditori Deo debitæ,in ten-tationis paroxysmo non admodum memorem esse:sed grauius est,errorum suorum & subsecutæ castigationis sic obliui-sci, ut nec offensam,nec eius austorame-tum (etsi huius sensus non multo ante a-cerbissimus fuit) agnoscas: ut grande παρα-[?] [?]παράπτωμα tuum opineris esse præclarum [?]κατόρθωμα[?]. Tertio loco subiungit eiusmodi misericordiæ & clementiæ diuinæ elogium, ut tamen specie quadam reprehensionis non careat. Enimuero stolidus & [illegible, ~9 letters] homuncio, Deo, quid eo dignum sit, indicare,& modum aliqueipsius clementiæ præscribere poterit,cum sibi præter meritum habito,uitilitigationis anfam exhibitam putabit. Tertius hic offensæ gradus fuit. Postremo,quasi homo sibi viuat & moriatur, & optimeno-ritu uitæ & mortis optima momenta, non autem ei uni à quo conditus est,mortem uitæ præfert, & à Deo se auocari ex hac vita cupide precatur. Fuit hic gradus quartus,de quo suo tempore,si volet Deo minus,dicam.Nunc enim illud fatis fue-rit ostedisse, etiam Sanctos interdum nō ex fide

page.notes: Several Greek words are doubtful: the hyphenated word at the line end ("παρα-"), the following word ("παράπτωμα"), the word "κατόρθωμα" and the word after "stolidus &" are uncertain or illegible in the scan. Where I could not read the Greek letter by letter, I marked it. The page number "335" is partly obscured and marked [?]. The word "uitilitigationis" is printed oddly and marked as uncertain in the text. The running head was changed from IONAE to JONAE (consonant J). The long s was changed to s throughout.
